document_title: Standards of Conduct for the International Civil Service / UN Ethics Framework
notes: UN Ethics Office established 2006. Five functions: advice; retaliation protection; financial disclosure; ethics training; standards coherence. Core values: integrity, professionalism, respect for diversity. ICSC Standards of Conduct govern all UN system staff. CROSS-LISTING from O84 (International Affairs/Public Administration). Policy portal: https://policy.un.org/en/accountability/ethical-standards-and-integrity

Standalone Code of Ethics (June 2020) separate from general UN framework. PDF: https://www.undp.org/sites/g/files/zskgke326/files/undp/library/corporate/ethics/UNDP%20CODE%20OF%20ETHICS%20-%20June%202020.pdf. Ethics Office: advice, retaliation protection, training, financial disclosure. POPP portal: https://popp.undp.org/accountability/ethics

document_title: IMF Code of Conduct for Staff
profession_name: IMF Staff / International Financial Institution Employee
notes: Covers all IMF employees. Separate Executive Board Code of Conduct at https://www.imf.org/external/hrd/edscode.htm. Ethical Conduct and Core Values Certification policy: https://www.imf.org/en/About/ethics-and-integrity/ethical-conduct-and-core-values-certification-and-financial-disclosure-policy-for-imf-staff. Annual ethics and integrity reports published publicly. Staff financial disclosure required.

document_title: World Bank Group Code of Ethics
profession_name: World Bank Group Staff / Development Finance Professional
notes: Core values: impact, integrity, respect, teamwork, innovation. PDF: https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/147281468337279671/pdf/WBG-Code-of-Ethics.pdf. Separate Board Officials Code of Conduct. INT (Integrity Vice Presidency) enforces. Whistleblower protections. Sanctions regime for misconduct.

Agreed by North Atlantic Council December 18, 2020. Applies to all NATO civilian and military staff across all NATO bodies. Core principles: integrity, loyalty, accountability, impartiality, professionalism. Read alongside NATO Civilian Personnel Regulations.

document_title: Code of Conduct for Members of the European Commission
notes: Updated 2018; covers all Commissioners during and after tenure (post-service restrictions, cooling-off periods). EC Staff ethics: https://commission.europa.eu/about/service-standards-and-principles/ethics-and-good-administration/staff-and-ethics_en. European Ombudsman oversees EU ethics: https://www.ombudsman.europa.eu/webpub/2024/ethics-standards/en/. Independent Ethical Committee enforces.

organization: International Committee of the Red Cross
document_title: Code of Conduct for Employees of the ICRC
notes: Covers internal ethical obligations of ICRC staff (integrity, accountability, humanitarian principles). PDF (2023): https://www.icrc.org/en/download/file/271318/code_of_conduct_2023.pdf. SEPARATE from the humanitarian sector-wide Code of Conduct for the International Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement and NGOs in Disaster Relief (IFRC, 1992): https://www.ifrc.org/document/code-conduct-international-red-cross-and-red-crescent-movement-and-ngos-disaster-relief. CROSS-LISTING from O84.

organization: Red Cross / Red Crescent Movement and NGOs
document_title: Code of Conduct for the International Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement and NGOs in Disaster Relief
notes: Drawn up 1992 by Steering Committee for Humanitarian Response (SCHR). Sets industry-wide ethical standards for humanitarian operations. Signed by major international humanitarian organizations. Foundational humanitarian sector ethics code. Distinct from the ICRC employee code (ISIC-U99-007) above.

document_title: UNESCO Ethics Office Handbook for Ethical Conduct
notes: UNESCO Ethics Office governs staff conduct. Handbook: https://unesdoc.unesco.org/ark:/48223/pf0000386038. Governed primarily by ICSC Standards with agency-specific guidance. 2021 Ethics Office Annual Report noted plans for UNESCO-specific Code of Conduct. CROSS-LISTING from P (Education) and O.

document_title: WTO Rules of Conduct for the Dispute Settlement Understanding
profession_name: WTO Panel Member / Arbitrator / Secretariat Staff
notes: Applies to panel members, Appellate Body members, experts, arbitrators, and WTO Secretariat staff in dispute settlement. WTO Ethics, Risk, and Compliance Office established September 2024 for broader staff ethics. General staff conduct governed by international civil service norms. Narrower scope than other UN system ethics codes.
